places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det ≈ 0.79224906 (a root of x³ − 20x² + 96x − 64) is real (numerically: |Im| < 10⁻¹⁰) and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.70637758π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 6; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.
